abstract: Intrinsic terminators are widely used in synthetic biology and metabolic engineering, yet their strength must be selected empirically from characterized libraries. We therefore developed a framework for designing intrinsic terminators with programmable strength. TK, designed to maximize termination strength, exceeded both B0010, a widely used standard, and the strongest terminator in a 582-member reference library when assayed in parallel. To establish that these gains reflect intrinsic termination rather than cellular context, we developed a cloning-free in vitro transcription assay using fluorescent light-up aptamers; TK again ranked highest. The framework improved the canonical T7 terminator and recovered strength rankings across three other bacterial species. Designs were generated using an interpretable sequence-to-function model trained from primary-sequence descriptors alone. The framework is available as open web tools, TerSP for strength prediction and TerFac for target-driven design. Model interpretation revealed previously unreported determinants, including a preference for compositionally diverse hairpin stems.
